The explorer who reached America in 1492 is Christopher Columbus.

Regarding the interplay between historical context and themes in *The Crucible*: Arthur Miller wrote the play in the 1950s, a period dominated by the Red Scare and McCarthyism. By setting the drama in the Salem witch trials of the 1690s, Miller creates a powerful allegory. The themes of mass hysteria, unfounded accusations, and the abuse of power mirror the political climate of the Cold War era. This parallel allows Miller to critique the irrational fear and destructive social dynamics of his own time, using the historical setting to highlight the dangers of ideological extremism and the erosion of civil liberties.
